purpose: OVERSEER. A third spec loop the operator asked for on 2026-09-07, after the first two completed: a system that connects to any AI harness, records what the agents are doing, and provides metrics and governance over them. New sibling project folder, spec loop inside it. This window proposes; it implements only the optional final skeleton, and only inside the new folder.
playbook: none -- one-off run. The queue below is the whole instruction. Round discipline is CLAUDE.md's.

queue.title: Spec loop R1 -- the overseer, in a new sibling folder
queue.detail: Read openspec/explorations/2026-09-07-an-overseer-for-any-harness.md FIRST. It is a seed: measurements to re-check, an honest assessment of the idea's risks, and questions you must ANSWER rather than inherit. Its central question is the one to settle before writing anything: is this a new product, or is it AgentWeave's Hub with the orchestration removed? The seed argues there IS a real distinction -- AgentWeave governs agents it spawns; an overseer governs agents it does not control -- but you must test that against the code rather than accept it. Your FIRST job is an inventory: what does AgentWeave already record, through what tables and what ingestion paths, and which of those are already reachable by a harness the Hub did not spawn. Then create the folder under C:\Users\huida\Documents\projects\, `git init` LOCALLY with no remote, scaffold openspec inside, and write the proposal there -- not in AgentWeave. Name the project yourself; 'overseer' is a working title, not a decision.
queue.result: witness created at C:/Users/huida/Documents/projects/witness (git init, no remote, commit 6b0a135). Inventory + proposal + design + tasks + 3 spec deltas; openspec validate --changes --strict passes. Framing settled AGAINST the seed's reason and FOR a stronger one: AgentWeave's security property is that identity is never accepted from a request, and an overseer's core operation is to accept a record about an actor it never authenticated. Measured: all 32 agent_actions routes gated on a run credential defined as a pointer into a runs row the Hub created; TurnUsage.run_id is a non-null unique FK with no HTTP writer, so cost is unreachable without a spawn; the 4 open ingestion routes require the INSTANCE-OPERATOR credential, not a project key (seed was wrong on both the paths and the auth model). Two seed corrections and two additions recorded: normalisation is NOT the gap (runner_parsing.py already does 3 harnesses), and the richest capture surface is the harness's own on-disk transcript, omitted from the seed's table -- 2,069 files / 985 MB on this machine, 17 record types, retroactive. Product commits to the passive lever and to no scoring; name carries the commitment. R1's own recommendation is propose-then-shelve pending 4 operator data-policy decisions.

queue.title: Spec loop R2 -- re-derive independently against AgentWeave's real recording layer
queue.detail: Not a re-read of R1. A fresh comparison against the code. For an extraction-adjacent proposal, R2's job is to compare it against THE THING IT DIFFERENTIATES FROM: read hub/hub/output_recording.py, the EventLog rows, the agent_outputs/runs/permission_requests/questions tables and the two compatibility self-report endpoints, and establish concretely how much of the proposed overseer AgentWeave already is. If the honest answer is 'most of it', say so -- that is a finding, not a failure, and it changes the proposal from a new product to a boundary question. Also check the seed's harness-capability table against anything in this repository that already parses or ingests a harness's output.

queue.title: Spec loop R3 -- re-derive again, and confront the enforcement question
queue.detail: Third pass, because unlike the continuity kit this proposal has a large body of existing code to be wrong about. Its specific job: the seed's hardest question, which R1 and R2 will both be tempted to defer. Recording is passive; GOVERNING is active, and on a harness you do not control the only levers are a gateway that can refuse, a tool-boundary hook that can refuse, or an after-the-fact report. Those are three different products with three different deployment stories. Establish which one the proposal actually commits to and make it say so in design.md. Also test the proposal against this repository's own stated principle -- the unasked-question backstop was retired 2026-08-20 because guessing intent from prose is a judgement the product should not make on the operator's behalf. An overseer that scores or judges agent behaviour runs straight into it.

queue.title: Append an overseer section to the existing review page
queue.detail: The operator reads ONE page. Append to .claude/autonomous/2026-09-07-sidequest-review.html rather than writing a second one, and while you are in there fix the header, which still says 'six iterations' and 'Eleven decisions' after S-10 made it eight and twelve. Same rules as before: self-contained, theme-aware, no external references, full wrapper kept. Say what each round CHANGED about the one before it; if a round changed nothing, say so. State plainly what could not be established without the open web or a running harness. Add the new decisions to the SQ series, continuing the numbering. Run scripts/drive/check_review_page.py and read its output rather than trusting its exit code.

queue.title: OPTIONAL -- the smallest runnable skeleton, and only if it can be driven
queue.detail: Only if T-4 is finished and more than 60 minutes remain before stop_at. The bar set by the continuity kit is the bar here: a skeleton that was DRIVEN against real data beat one that merely existed, because driving it produced a sixth failure mode and a spec defect nobody had reasoned their way to. So build only what can be pointed at something real and run -- this machine has a genuine corpus of agent activity in .claude/autonomous/*-log.md, driver logs, git history and scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md. Do NOT start a Hub, do NOT run an agent turn, do NOT touch AgentWeave product code. If nothing can be driven within the time, skip this item and say why rather than shipping an undriven skeleton.

decisions_for_user.question: May Witness read the local Claude Code transcript corpus at all?
decisions_for_user.evidence: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl is 2,069 files and 985 MB of your real sessions, containing prompts, source code, tool arguments and plausibly credentials, complete and unredacted. Unlike every OTel surface (where content is off until five flags are set), there is no vendor-side default withholding anything. It is also the ONLY surface that is retroactive -- it covers sessions that ran before the tool existed, which is all 2,069 of them. There is no partial answer that keeps the retroactive property.
decisions_for_user.blocks: Every phase of tasks.md except phase 0.

decisions_for_user.question: Redaction posture: at read, at write, or not at all?
decisions_for_user.evidence: At read loses fidelity permanently and makes the record less useful for the incident it was built for. At write leaves a window. Not at all makes the Witness store the most sensitive file on the machine. AgentWeave's redact_secrets (runner_events.py:63) is a working starting point either way.

decisions_for_user.question: Retention period for the record store.
decisions_for_user.evidence: A record that answers 'what did the agents do last quarter' must be kept for a quarter. That is a different risk profile from a debugging aid kept for a week.

decisions_for_user.question: Who may read the record -- you only, or anyone else?
decisions_for_user.evidence: Single-operator local is the first cut's assumption. The moment a second reader exists this becomes an access-control product and the scope roughly triples.

decisions_for_user.question: Does the name 'witness' survive?
decisions_for_user.evidence: Chosen because it commits the product to the passive posture -- a witness testifies to what it saw and is expected to say what it did not see. If a later round decides the product must enforce, the name must change too. Whether it collides with an existing project could not be checked offline.
